issue.title: Notebook and Prose Cards have no visible-body Vim guard, and home/Ref cards carry two divergent guard designs

task_type_fields.impact: In a Vim-mode Notebook or Prose note, a routine upward motion can put the cursor (and any following edit) inside hidden frontmatter or the hidden title. Typing there edits YAML or the H1 the user cannot see. Two divergent guard implementations also make the next family card likely to ship without one.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins plugins/bob-ledger-tools/src/249i-plugin-notebook-card-host.js and 249n-plugin-prose-note-card-host.js (no visible-body navigation guard); compare 249db-plugin-home-card-vim-navigation.js and 249w-plugin-ref-note-card-vim-navigation.js
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by bob-cli-qp.7 (note #4, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP) and triaged by the bob-cli-qp land agent.

The Notebook Card and the Prose Card hide the note's frontmatter and, like the other title-owning cards, a matching first H1. Neither card host registers a visible-body navigation guard. On bob-plugins master (28e75739), no fragment other than the home card (249d/249db) and the Ref Card (249s/249w) references `homeCardVisibleBodyLine` or any `*VisibleBodyNavigation` handler. With Vim on, `gg`, `k`, or Up from the first body line of a Notebook or Prose note can therefore move the cursor into hidden frontmatter or the hidden title line. This is the same class of defect the home-card and Ref Card guards exist to prevent.

The family now has two guard designs:
- 249db (home card) intercepts keys through CodeMirror and swallows them. In real Obsidian, Vim sees the keydown first, so 0ffb4511 (bob-cli-qi) had to add `homeCardCancelPendingVimInput` to clear a pending `g`, count, or operator after a swallowed key.
- 249w (Ref Card, bob-cli-qp.7 repair in 2bd92b19) listens on the document in the capture phase, lets Vim finish its own motion so Vim's pending state stays consistent, then clamps the cursor to the body start on the next frame. In qp.7's real-Obsidian acceptance it proved `gg`/`k`/Up on Ref Cards (54/54 GO).

Repro (real Obsidian, Vim mode on): open a Notebook note or a Prose note that has a Notebook/Prose Card and a matching H1, put the cursor on the first visible body line, and press `k` or `gg`. Expected: the cursor stays on the first visible body line. Suspected: it lands on a hidden line. Confirm with the takeover or home-cards runner before fixing.

Remediation: put one shared kit helper in the property-card kit, using the proven 249w capture-and-clamp design and the shared `homeCardVisibleBodyLine`. Register it for home, Notebook, Prose, and Ref cards, then delete the per-species copies. Real-Obsidian proof: `gg`, `k`, and Up on each species, `==` still opening Settings after `gg`, and no pending Vim operator left armed.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-qp.7's real-Obsidian Ref Card acceptance found that the home-card guard design does not engage under Obsidian Vim and that Notebook and Prose cards have no guard at all; the Ref Cards epic fixed only its own species.
